Hello, newbie here. I saw Mathlib currently has no Bessel functions (please correct me if I am wrong), and I have an axiom-free development of the Bessel function of the first kind of integer order. Is there any interest in such PR?
It's defined by its power series Jₙ(x) = ∑ₘ (-1)ᵐ / (m!·(m+n)!) · (x/2)^(2m+n) (as per DLMF §10.2.2), and so far includes:

  • summability / entireness, values at 0, parity Jₙ(-x) = (-1)ⁿ Jₙ(x)
  • hasDerivAt_besselJ (term-by-term differentiation, via hasDerivAt_tsum)
  • the three-term recurrences, the derivative-product relations
This topic was moved here from #general > Bessel functions by Michael Rothgang.
I'd be more than happy to review it to the best of my abilities, and I don't think it's controversial that they belong in mathlib

I also have some code about Bessel functions in my mathlib fork ("bessel" branch) and I was somewhat planning to upstream it after my current PR queue is shortened. I wouldn't mind it if someone else PR it first. Could you take a look and see if there is anything from my code you can take?

Sure can do, let me have a look at it, thank you for your reply

I agree that Bessel functions should be in mathlib, in some form. However I will caution as usual that llm-generated code is typically not useful for mathlib, unless after careful and thorough review.

I don't think that non-negative integers as the parameter is the right thing to do. Without any problems you should be able to take the gamma function docs#Complex.Gamma. Also I would expect it to be more useful to define 0F1{}_0F_10​F1​ first (even better: define pFq{}_pF_qp​Fq​, but restrict all of the proofs whenever necessary) and then deduce all of the properties of $$J_\alpha$ from that.
I also very much agree with Bhavik: getting these definitions right is not as easy as pointing a large language model to dlmf and hoping for the best.
I tried using hypergeometric functions in my attempt, but they behave badly for negative integers due to 0/0. My version ended up using power series but still allows complex \alpha

That is annoying, I assume the 0/0 comes from the gamma functions? I wonder whether there is some way of dealing with cancellation of poles and zeros in a way that does not involve redefining very similar functions all of the time. You did have some code for equality up to a discrete set? Can't you use that to define a holomorphic function from a function with only removable singularities?
I don't know whether it is worth it in this case to jump through these extra hoops, though

Bhavik Mehta said:

I agree that Bessel functions should be in mathlib, in some form. However I will caution as usual that llm-generated code is typically not useful for mathlib, unless after careful and thorough review.

Indeed, I assumed this was human or "human + careful AI use" generated code. @Sorin Suciu this is the case right?

@Moritz Doll indeed it comes from both gamma functions and 0F1. The expression is like 0F1/\Gamma(\alpha +1). They are both globally junk zero for all x when \alpha is a negative integer so if one wants to argue about removable singularity, they need to use the holomorphicity on \alpha
Formula from wikipedia

I guess that having the extra factor of Γ(α+1)−1\Gamma(\alpha+1)^{-1}Γ(α+1)−1 is not too bad. You could then define 0F1{}_0F_10​F1​ as Γ(α+1)\Gamma(\alpha+1)Γ(α+1) times that function and there the value is junk anyway (because it is a pole).

Hi guys,
Yes, it is human crafted and LLM was just used for proving some identities and code review. But examining Weiyi's code, I realized it is better than what I did (on mine there's no integral representation, generating function, analyticity), so I will rest my case here, hope he will find time to issue the PR, and I will happily use it.
Thank you all for being helpful and friendly.
For the Gauss hypergeometric function, there is also a tendency to use Γ(c)−12F1(a,b;c;z)\Gamma(c)^{-1}{}_2F_1(a, b;c;z)Γ(c)−12​F1​(a,b;c;z), so maybe that is generally the right move.
do we have Γ(z)−1\Gamma(z)^{-1}Γ(z)−1 as a function with no junk values? It's holomorphic everywhere, right?
Can't you just take the inverse of Gamma? I think the Gamma function is zero at its poles, so it's inverse will have the correct values everywhere?
docs#Complex.Gamma_neg_nat_eq_zero
And we have docs#Complex.differentiable_one_div_Gamma

Γ(z)−1\Gamma(z)^{-1}Γ(z)−1 itself is fine here. What we need is to let its zero cancel the pole of 0F1{}_0 F_10​F1​ and get a non-zero value. I am not familiar with the convention of generalized hypergeometric function. I haven't found materials that bundle Γ(z)−10F1(−;z;x)\Gamma(z)^{-1} {}_0 F_1 (-;z;x)Γ(z)−10​F1​(−;z;x) as one function

In comparison, the power series definition of Bessel function J doesn't need to case-split on negative integers, though it (ab)uses junk value Γ(m+α+1)−1=0\Gamma(m + \alpha + 1)^{-1} = 0Γ(m+α+1)−1=0 in the first few terms for negative integer α\alphaα

@Weiyi Wang I just had a look into your code and it is basically what I was going for. Here is what I had in mind (adapted from your code):

module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Gamma.Digamma

@[expose] public noncomputable section

namespace Complex

open scoped Nat Real
open Topology Filter

def gammaRatio (a z : ℂ) : ℂ := toMeromorphicNFOn (fun s ↦ Gamma (a + s) / Gamma s) Set.univ z

theorem gammaRatio_eq_ratio (a z : ℂ) (h : ∀ n : ℕ, a + z ≠ -n) :
    gammaRatio a z = Gamma (a + z) / Gamma z := by sorry -- I have a proof

variable {p q : ℕ}

variable {a : Fin p → ℂ} {b : Fin q → ℂ}

def regularizedHGFunSeries (a : Fin p → ℂ) (b : Fin q → ℂ) :
    FormalMultilinearSeries ℂ ℂ ℂ :=
  .ofScalars ℂ fun n ↦ (n ! * ∏ j : Fin q, Gamma (b j + n))⁻¹ * (∏ i : Fin p, gammaRatio n (a i))

theorem radius_regularizedHGFunSeries (a : Fin p → ℂ) (b : Fin q → ℂ) (h : p < q + 1) :
    (regularizedHGFunSeries a b).radius = ⊤ := by
  sorry
  -- should be very similar, with slightly more involved calculation

@[simp]
theorem regularizedHGFunSeries_p_eq_zero (a : Fin 0 → ℂ) (b : Fin q → ℂ) :
    regularizedHGFunSeries a b = .ofScalars ℂ fun n ↦ (n ! * ∏ j : Fin q, Gamma (b j + n))⁻¹ := by
  unfold regularizedHGFunSeries
  simp

def besselJ (a x : ℂ) :=
  (x / 2) ^ a * regularizedHGFun (fun _ : Fin 0 ↦ 0) (fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ a) (-(x / 2) ^ 2)

theorem besselJ_int_neg (a : ℤ) (x : ℂ) :
    besselJ a (-x) = (-1) ^ a * besselJ a x := by
  unfold besselJ
  simp_rw [cpow_intCast, neg_div, neg_sq, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_zpow, neg_one_mul]

def besselI (a x : ℂ) :=
  (x / 2) ^ a * regularizedHGFun (fun _ : Fin 0 ↦ 0) (fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ a) ((x / 2) ^ 2)

theorem besselI_int_neg (a : ℤ) (x : ℂ) :
    besselI a (-x) = (-1) ^ a * besselI a x := by
  unfold besselI
  simp_rw [cpow_intCast, neg_div, neg_sq, ← mul_assoc, ← mul_zpow, neg_one_mul]
